land.text: the Ua Conchobair remnant around Roscommon; Connacht 'was shired into its present counties' in the late 1500s under the Tudor conquest

successors.note: The rest of Connacht passed to the de Burgh lordship in 1235 (Lordship of Ireland).

capitals.name: Rathcroghan (Cruachan)
capitals.note: The Connacht article gives 'Rathcroghan in north County Roscommon' as the O Conor base by 1050; the page gives no years for the seat. Coordinates are the researcher's.

correction.text: the Connachta base: 'By 1050, they had extended their rule from Rathcroghan in north County Roscommon'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Connacht. The page gives the Connachta core at Rathcroghan before 1050 and no earlier boundary; the old province Coiced Ol nEchmacht may have been larger. No area given.

correction.text: large areas of Galway, Mayo, Sligo and Leitrim as well as Roscommon: the five modern counties of Connacht

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'At its greatest extent, it incorporated the often independent Kingdom of Breifne, as well as vassalage from the lordships of western Mide and west Leinster'; the greatest extent is undated on the page (Tairrdelbach and Ruaidri were High Kings in the 12th century), so Breifne and the vassal lands are not added.

correction.text: the five cantreds in Roscommon left to Feidlim Ua Conchobair: 'allowed to hold only five cantreds'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the rump kingdom after Richard de Burgh's conquest, 'held ... of the crown of England' as a vassal of the Lordship. The five cantreds are drawn as County Roscommon, which is larger than they were.

region.text: the Connachta around Rathcroghan, descended from Brion, Ailill and Fiachrae

ledger.note: The Connachta: 'a group of dynasties who claimed descent from the three eldest sons of Eochaid Mugmedon'; their younger brother Niall, ancestor of the Ui Neill, 'died c. 450/455', and the king list runs 'from the fifth to fifteenth centuries'. The page gives no founding year; 450 is the researcher's bridge.

region.text: 'large areas of what are now County Galway, County Mayo, County Sligo, and County Leitrim'

ledger.note: By 1050: the Ui Briuin extend from Rathcroghan over the rest of the province. 'By 1050, they had extended their rule from Rathcroghan in north County Roscommon' over those counties. The page names no state they took it from, hence nobody.

region.text: Connacht but for the five cantreds: 'Richard held the remaining 25 cantreds of Connacht in chief of the crown of England'

ledger.note: 1235: Richard Mor de Burgh conquers Connacht. 'It was only in 1235 ... that he finally expelled the Gaelic king'; Feidlim 'was obliged to pay homage and was allowed to hold only five cantreds'. The Connacht article gives 1237 for the start of encastellation and says the kingdom 'collapsed in the 1230s because of civil war within the royal dynasty'; granted to Richard in May 1227.

region.text: the five cantreds left to Feidlim Ua Conchobair in Roscommon

ledger.note: [Reviewer eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Mirror of lordship-of-ireland's 1235 vassal_start. 'It was only in 1235' that Richard Mór de Burgh 'finally expelled the Gaelic king'; Felim 'was obliged to pay homage' and was 'allowed to hold only five cantreds' in Roscommon (Richard Mór de Burgh page).

region.text: the Ua Conchobair remnant in Roscommon

ledger.note: [Reviewer eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Mirror of lordship-of-ireland's 1474 vassal_end: the kingship was held by the Ó Conchobair line 'until the death of the last king in 1474' (Connacht page); the end of the dependence is the end of the kingship.

1474: the last king dies. 'From then until the death of the last king in 1474, the kingship was held exclusively by the O Conchobair's.' The lead of the same page puts the collapse of the kingdom in the 1230s, so 1474 ends only the title. [Reviewer eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Counterpart was kingdom-of-ireland, which begins only on 18 June 1542 (Kingdom of Ireland page, Crown of Ireland Act); in 1474 the overlord and successor is the Lordship of Ireland.

wars.name: Norman conquest of Connacht
wars.outcome: Raided by the Normans in 1177; Richard Mor de Burgh, granted Connacht in May 1227, expelled Feidlim in 1235 and left him five cantreds; encastellation began in 1237.
wars.note: Dates: raid 1177 and 1237 from the Connacht article, 1227 and 1235 from the de Burgh article.

wars.name: Ruaidri Ua Conchobair against the Normans

zones.text: Meath, from which he 'drove the Normans out' and burned Trim and Kells

wars.outcome: High King from 1166; signed the Treaty of Windsor with Henry II in 1175; 'abdicated in 1183, but returned to rule briefly twice'; died 2 December 1198.
wars.note: The page gives no dates for the Meath campaign.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary; the province and the Roscommon core are the only anchors.

notes: The Kingdom of Connacht page is a stub (origins and a king list); the Connacht province page carries the history. Start 450 is a bridge (confidence 1). The kingdom's collapse is dated 1235 (de Burgh) while the title lasted to 1474; the Lordship dossier should carry a vassal_start 1235 and vassal_end 1474 for the Roscommon remnant. After 1333 the Burkes (Clanricarde, Mayo) split Connacht; the O Conor kings are not a state of their own after 1474. Breifne (the Ui Ruairc kingdom) needs its own dossier if a group wants it. The Composition of Connacht (1585) was not opened.
